**Test image observations:**
- Dense white cottony/fluffy mycelium densely wrapped around the stem crown at the soil line junction

- Classic presentation of a stem-base fungal pathogen

**Comparison summary:**
- **Southern_Blight**: Reference images 5411390/5411388 show white cottony mycelium at soil line/stem crown — **best match**
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Shows white mycelium but with prominent large black sclerotia not visible in test image
- **Gray_Mold**: Shows gray (not white) mold primarily on fruit/stem junctions — no match

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Bacterial streaming, no mycelium — no match
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: V-shaped leaf lesions and vascular streaking — no match
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Dark cankers, some grayish coating but no dense white mycelium — no match

The dense white cottony mycelium at the stem crown/soil line is the hallmark sign of **Southern_Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*).
